_meta.based_on: Public handbooks of GitLab and Sourcegraph, plus common lost-device and on-call phone practices. Each rule's 'source' says where it comes from; 'assumption' means invented for this lab.

tool_mapping.get_employee_info(employee_id): employees.json -> role, tenure (from hire_date), status, on_call, equipment on file, peripheral_spend
tool_mapping.get_policy_limits(role): roles[role] -> laptop_tier, laptop_refresh_months (how often), peripheral budgets (how much per year), entitlements (what)
tool_mapping.check_request_eligibility(employee_id, i: item = a category ('laptop', 'monitor', 'security_key', ...) or a SKU ('LAP-PRO16-64') or 'personal_laptop'. request_type = standard | broken | lost | additional | keep_after_leaving. Runs rules 1-14 in order; first rule that decides wins. Returns decision, rule id, reason, and any computed values (eligible_date, remaining_budget).
tool_mapping.flag_for_human_review(employee_id, reque: appends one JSON line to escalations.jsonl

intern.note: Laptop must be returned at the end of the internship.

contractor.note: Contractors without a company laptop may be issued one security key for SSO login. A company laptop is an exception that needs IT + Security approval.

rules.check: Employment status. terminated -> deny. on_leave -> escalate. offboarding -> deny any request except request_type 'keep_after_leaving'
Item is known. 'personal_laptop' -> deny (personal laptops may not be used for company work). Item not in catalog -> escalate

request_type 'lost' for a laptop or phone -> escalate as a security incident: employee reports to IT and manager in writing within 24 hours, files a police report within 72 hours if stolen, IT remote-wipes the device
request_type 'broken' for a laptop -> escalate: early replacement goes through the replacement program, where IT assesses repair vs replace
request_type 'additional' for a laptop -> escalate: a second device needs a business justification plus manager approval and IT approval

request_type 'keep_after_leaving' (keep laptop at offboarding). Requires status offboarding. If offboarding_for_cause -> deny. If the laptop has been in use >= 12 months -> approve (kept at no cost after IT wipes it). Otherwise -> deny (may buy it at current net value instead)
Contractor requesting a laptop -> escalate: contractors are a listed exception needing IT + Security approval

Entitlement. laptop: role has a laptop_tier. Peripherals: role peripheral_scope is 'all', or 'electronic_only' and the item is an electronic peripheral. security_key: security_keys_max > 0. mobile_phone: employee on_call is true. Otherwise -> deny
rules.source: assumption, modeled on https://about.sourcegraph.com/handbook/people-ops/spending-company-money (intern budget covers electronic desk items only) and UM-Dearborn phone criteria (on-call staff)

rules.check: Laptop spec. If a specific laptop SKU is requested and its tier ranks above the role's laptop_tier -> escalate (higher spec needs prior approval)

Laptop refresh. No active laptop on file -> approve (new issue at role tier). Otherwise months since in_use_since >= laptop_refresh_months -> approve; else deny and return eligible_date = in_use_since + refresh months. The clock starts when the laptop went into active use, not hire date

Security key. If request_type is 'lost' but no key on file has status 'reported_lost' -> escalate (the lost key must be reported and revoked before a replacement ships). Otherwise active keys < security_keys_max -> approve; else deny
Mobile phone (on-call already confirmed by rule 9). Already has an active company phone -> deny; else approve

Peripheral budget. Tenure < 12 months: remaining = first_year budget minus all spend since hire. Tenure >= 12 months: remaining = annual budget minus spend dated within the 12 months before as_of. Item price <= remaining -> approve; else escalate (over budget needs manager approval)

standing_facts.old_laptop_handback: After receiving a refreshed laptop, the old one must be wiped or returned within 2 weeks (GitLab).
standing_facts.mdm_required: All company laptops are enrolled in device management (MDM) and can be remotely wiped (GitLab).
standing_facts.company_property: Physical items over $1,000 are company property (Sourcegraph).
standing_facts.two_keys_why: Two security keys are issued so a lost key doesn't lock the employee out while a replacement ships (Sourcegraph).
